essentialIdeas: Use the product rule for a product of two functions: the derivative is first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first.
Use the chain rule for a composite function: differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.

methodBriefing.what: Study a correct model, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, and explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining and repairing helps turn a rule into a usable mental model.

activities.label: Product rule model
activities.title: Product rule pattern
activities.body: Read the model and watch the example structure. Then move on to the check.

essentialIdeas: Use the product rule for a product of two functions: the derivative is first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first.

activities.label: Product rule recall
activities.title: Say the product rule
activities.body: State the rule in your own words. Keep it to one clear attempt.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: For a product of two functions, the derivative is first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and the plus sign. If you only differentiate one factor, repair that missing second term.

activities.label: Product rule repair
activities.title: Fix the product step
activities.body: Correct the missing piece in your rule. Then give the full rule again.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Differentiating a product means differentiating only one factor.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product uses both terms: first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first.
activities.feedback: The fix is to include both factors. A one-sided derivative is incomplete for a product.

activities.label: Chain rule model
activities.title: Chain rule pattern
activities.body: Read the model and note the inner and outer roles. Then move on to the check.

essentialIdeas: Use the chain rule for a composite function: differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.

activities.label: Chain rule recall
activities.title: Say the chain rule
activities.body: Explain the rule in plain words from memory. Then check your wording against the model.
activities.concept: Chain rule
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, differentiate the outer function and multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
activities.feedback: A complete answer includes both parts: outer derivative and inner derivative. If you leave out the inner derivative, the chain is broken.

activities.label: Chain rule recognition
activities.title: Recognize the chain rule
activities.body: Choose the best description of the chain rule. One answer only.
activities.concept: Chain rule
choices: Differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
Differentiate each part of a sum and add the results.
Differentiate only the inside function and stop.
Multiply two derivatives whenever a function is written inside parentheses.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
activities.feedback: The chain rule links an outer derivative to an inner derivative. It is for composition, not simple sums or isolated inside terms.
